topic.title: What if a bridge joined Russia and America?
topic.map_answer: the Bering Strait between Russia's Chukotka and Alaska: about 82 km of sea with the two Diomede islands in the middle, 3.8 km apart, the International Date Line running between them

shape.name: The crossing
shape.beats: hook: the two giants on the globe and the question -> how near they really are at one strait, a figure -> the two islands in the middle and whose each is -> how shallow the sea is -> build it: the bridge hops island to island -> drive it end to end across two continents, country by country -> the real plan that stalled -> payoff: the date line between the islands, a drive into yesterday -> loop back to the globe
shape.why: a what-if whose answer is one narrow gap on the map: dive from space onto the strait, span it, then pull back to drive the new road across the world

title: What if you could drive from Russia to Alaska?
description:
Russia and Alaska sit across one narrow strait. What if a road crossed it?
The Bering Strait on the map: two islands in the middle, a bridge hopping between them, and a drive from London to New York.
Sources: Wikipedia, Bering Strait and Diomede Islands (Nov 2026). The characters are not advisers.
Maps simplified. Borders as recognised by the country each video is about.
